components.note: 子 (child) — children and offspring, as in 孙 grandchild, 学 study, 字 character; 孩 is a young child.
亥 (hài) is a close sound clue for hái; 亥 also sounds out 该 gāi, 核 hé and 刻 kè.
儿 (child, legs) — shows a person's legs; in 兒 the top was a child's soft skull. As an ending (这儿) it adds the er sound; 儿 also in 先, 兄, 光.

example.hanzi: 这孩儿长得真可爱。
example.pinyin: Zhè háir zhǎng de zhēn kě'ài.
example.english: This child is really adorable.
example.fact: Human infants are born with a reflexive grasp strong enough to briefly support their own body weight if they cling to a bar or a finger. Researchers consider it a holdover from primate ancestors, whose newborns needed to grip their mother's fur to avoid falling as she moved.

examples.hanzi: 这孩儿真聪明。
examples.pinyin: Zhè háir zhēn cōngming.
examples.english: This kid is really smart.

examples.hanzi: 你家那孩儿多大了？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiā nà háir duō dà le?
examples.english: How old is that child of yours?

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 播 is scattering seed by hand, then broadcasting.
番 (fān) — near sound — 播 is bō; 番 also sounds out 翻 fān and 潘 pān.

example.hanzi: 电视台正在播新闻。
example.pinyin: Diànshìtái zhèngzài bō xīnwén.
example.english: The TV station is broadcasting the news.
example.fact: The original sense is 'to sow seeds', and the idea of scattering carried over to broadcasting. Today 播 is everywhere in media words: 播放 (play), 广播 (radio) and 直播 (livestream).

examples.hanzi: 电台每天早上播音乐。
examples.pinyin: Diàntái měitiān zǎoshang bō yīnyuè.
examples.english: The radio station plays music every morning.

examples.hanzi: 农民在春天播种。
examples.pinyin: Nóngmín zài chūntiān bōzhǒng.
examples.english: Farmers sow seeds in spring.

components.note: 寸 (hand, inch) — hands and measuring, as in 寻 seek, 导 lead, 射 shoot; 对 faces someone or matches a pair. 又 here only stands in for the left side of 對.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 话 is speech.
舌 (shé, tongue) fits the meaning (speaking) and is a loose sound clue for huà; also in 活 huó.

example.hanzi: 两国代表进行了长时间的对话。
example.pinyin: Liǎng guó dàibiǎo jìnxíng le cháng shíjiān de duìhuà.
example.english: Representatives of the two countries held a lengthy dialogue.
example.fact: The Turing Test, proposed by mathematician Alan Turing in 1950, judges machine intelligence purely through open-ended conversation: if a human judge cannot reliably tell whether they're talking to a person or a machine, the machine is said to have passed. Turing originally called it 'the imitation game.'

examples.hanzi: 我们需要和客户对话。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào hé kèhù duìhuà.
examples.english: We need to have a dialogue with our client.

examples.hanzi: 这篇课文是两个人的对话。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān kèwén shì liǎng ge rén de duìhuà.
examples.english: This text is a conversation between two people.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and discussion: 说, 议, 谈; 论 is debate and theory.
仑 (lún) gives the sound; same part in 轮 lún and 伦 lún.

example.hanzi: 不论天气如何,比赛都会照常进行。
example.pinyin: Bùlùn tiānqì rúhé, bǐsài dōu huì zhàocháng jìnxíng.
example.english: No matter what the weather is like, the match will go on as scheduled.
example.fact: The speed of light in a vacuum measures the same for every observer, no matter how fast they themselves are moving — a strange, experimentally confirmed fact that forms the foundation of Einstein's theory of special relativity. Accepting it forces time itself to run at different rates for observers moving relative to one another.

examples.hanzi: 不论多难，我都要试一试。
examples.pinyin: Bùlùn duō nán, wǒ dōu yào shì yi shì.
examples.english: No matter how hard it is, I'm going to give it a try.

examples.hanzi: 不论你去哪儿，我都支持你。
examples.pinyin: Bùlùn nǐ qù nǎr, wǒ dōu zhīchí nǐ.
examples.english: No matter where you go, I'll support you.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — marks borders and boundaries, as in 国 country, 园 garden; 圆 is a round enclosed shape.
员 (yuán) — same sound: 圆 yuán. 员 also sounds out 韵 yùn and 陨 yǔn.

example.hanzi: 今晚的月亮又大又圆。
example.pinyin: Jīnwǎn de yuèliang yòu dà yòu yuán.
example.english: Tonight the moon is big and round.
example.fact: Roundness symbolises completeness in Chinese culture, which is why 团圆 means a family reunion and the round full moon of Mid-Autumn is tied to togetherness. 圆 is also the formal way to write the currency unit 元 in some contexts.

examples.hanzi: 他用铅笔画了一个很圆的圈。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng qiānbǐ huà le yí ge hěn yuán de quān.
examples.english: He drew a very round circle with a pencil.

examples.hanzi: 这张桌子是圆的,可以坐十个人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhuōzi shì yuán de, kěyǐ zuò shí ge rén.
examples.english: This table is round and seats ten people.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 钅 is the simplified 金 (metal), as in 钱, 铁; 镇 first meant to weigh down with metal.
真 (zhēn) — near sound — 镇 is zhèn; 真 also sounds out 慎 shèn and 填 tián.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 镇上新开了一家咖啡馆。
example.pinyin: Zhènshàng xīn kāi le yì jiā kāfēiguǎn.
example.english: A new café just opened in town.
example.fact: The small Austrian town of Hallstatt lent its name to an entire early Iron Age European culture after 19th-century archaeologists uncovered thousands of ancient graves near its salt mines. The Hallstatt culture, dated roughly 800 to 450 BC, is now used by historians across Europe as a reference point for that era.

examples.hanzi: 镇上的人都认识他。
examples.pinyin: Zhèn shàng de rén dōu rènshi tā.
examples.english: Everyone in town knows him.

examples.hanzi: 我们去镇上买点菜吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen qù zhèn shàng mǎi diǎn cài ba.
examples.english: Let's go into town to buy some groceries.

components.note: 戈 (halberd) — a weapon radical, as in 战 war and 成. 我 began as a picture of a jagged-bladed weapon; the pronoun "I" is a later borrowing of the sound.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.hanzi: 欢迎你随时来我家做客。
example.pinyin: Huānyíng nǐ suíshí lái wǒjiā zuòkè.
example.english: You're welcome to visit my home anytime.
example.fact: Termite mounds function like a natural climate-control system: their internal network of tunnels channels air currents that keep the colony's core temperature stable within a degree or two, even as the outside temperature swings by more than 20 degrees Celsius between night and day.

examples.hanzi: 我家离学校很近。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lí xuéxiào hěn jìn.
examples.english: My home is very close to school.

examples.hanzi: 我家有三口人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒjiā yǒu sān kǒu rén.
examples.english: There are three people in my family.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
女 (woman) — female kin and women: 妈 mom, 姐 sister, 妹 younger sister, 娘; 姑 is a father's sister.
古 (gǔ) is close to gū; the series includes 估 gū, 枯 kū, 苦 kǔ and 故 gù.
女 (woman) — mothers and girls: 妈, 姑, 姐; 娘 is mother or young woman, as in 新娘 bride.
良 (liáng) is a loose sound hint (-iang); same part in 狼 láng and 浪 làng.

example.hanzi: 那个小姑娘正在公园里荡秋千。
example.pinyin: Nàge xiǎogūniang zhèngzài gōngyuán lǐ dàng qiūqiān.
example.english: That little girl is swinging on the swing in the park.
example.fact: Malala Yousafzai was just 15 years old when she survived an assassination attempt for publicly advocating girls' right to education in Pakistan. Two years later, at age 17, she became the youngest person ever to receive the Nobel Peace Prize.

examples.hanzi: 这个小姑娘今年五岁。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎo gūniang jīnnián wǔ suì.
examples.english: This little girl is five years old.

examples.hanzi: 小姑娘穿着一条红裙子。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo gūniang chuān zhe yì tiáo hóng qúnzi.
examples.english: The little girl is wearing a red skirt.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks water and sinking, as in 海, 没 sink, 游; 沉 is to sink.
冗 (rǒng) is only a loose sound hint for chén.
黑 (black) — marks darkness, as in 墨 ink, 黯 dim; 默 mò (silent) sounds like 墨 mò, with 犬 dog quietly following.

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息后,他陷入了沉默。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi hòu, tā xiànrù le chénmò.
example.english: After hearing the news, he fell into silence.
example.fact: An anechoic chamber at Orfield Labs in Minnesota holds the Guinness World Record for the quietest place on Earth, absorbing over 99.99% of sound. Visitors report being able to hear their own heartbeat and blood flow once inside, and most people can't tolerate sitting in total silence for more than 45 minutes.

examples.hanzi: 大家都沉默了，没有人说话。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu chénmò le, méiyǒu rén shuōhuà.
examples.english: Everyone fell silent, and nobody spoke.

examples.hanzi: 他是个沉默寡言的人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge chénmò guǎyán de rén.
examples.english: He is a person of few words.

components.note: 讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talk, as in 说, 语, 讲; 详 is a full account, in detail.
羊 (yáng) hints at the sound: 详 xiáng is close, as in 祥 xiáng and 洋 yáng.
纟 (silk, thread) — simplified 糸; thread is the classic fine thing, so 细 means thin, slender, then detailed — as in 线 line, 红 red.

example.hanzi: 请把事情的经过详细地说一遍。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shìqing de jīngguò xiángxì de shuō yí biàn.
example.english: Please describe what happened in detail.
example.fact: NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter has photographed the Moon's surface in such fine detail that individual bootprints left by Apollo astronauts more than 50 years ago are still clearly visible in its images, along with the paths of the rovers they drove.

examples.hanzi: 请详细介绍一下你的计划。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng xiángxì jièshào yíxià nǐ de jìhuà.
examples.english: Please introduce your plan in detail.

examples.hanzi: 这份报告写得很详细。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn bàogào xiě de hěn xiángxì.
examples.english: This report is written in great detail.

components.note: 厂 (cliff) — the visible frame, as in 原, 厚. Memory aid: a stern cliff face — 严重 serious, 严格 strict. Cliff family hint, not proven.
嚴 (traditional) — a larger shape with two mouths 吅 shouting orders. 严 cut it to 亚 plus 厂, losing the clue.
肀 (brush in hand) — the top part and radical, a hand holding a tool. 肃 is simplified from 肅; Memory aid: a hand quietly holding a brush, serious and solemn as in 严肃.

example.hanzi: 老师用严肃的语气警告了我们。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī yòng yánsù de yǔqì jǐnggào le wǒmen.
example.english: The teacher warned us in a serious tone.
example.fact: The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery has been guarded around the clock, in every kind of weather, without a single interruption since 1937. Sentinels follow a precisely choreographed 21-step walk across the plaza, a number chosen to echo the 21-gun salute, the highest military honor.

examples.hanzi: 他的表情很严肃。
examples.pinyin: Tā de biǎoqíng hěn yánsù.
examples.english: His expression is very serious.

examples.hanzi: 这是一个严肃的问题，不能开玩笑。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí ge yánsù de wèntí, bù néng kāi wánxiào.
examples.english: This is a serious matter, so don't joke about it.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 女 marks women and feelings in old forms, as in 妒, 嫉; 嫌 is to dislike.
兼 (jiān) — near sound — 嫌 is xián; 兼 also sounds out 谦 qiān and 歉 qiàn.
疋 (foot) — the lower right. Dictionary story: an old man walking 疋 with a cane. Early forms show a person looking around, unsure. Treat as a memory aid.
矢 (arrow) — Dictionary reads it as a cane held by an old man; memory aid: an old man leaning on a stick, unsure which way — doubt, 怀疑.
犭 (beast, form of 犬 dog) — animals: 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狼 wolf; 犯 is to attack or violate, hence offend.

example.hanzi: 警方逮捕了一名嫌疑犯。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng dàibǔ le yì míng xiányífàn.
example.english: The police arrested a suspect.
example.fact: Fingerprint evidence became a standard tool in criminal investigation only in the early 1900s. One landmark case came in 1892, when Argentine police official Juan Vucetich matched a bloody fingerprint at a crime scene to a suspect, producing the first criminal conviction in history based on fingerprint identification.

examples.hanzi: 警察正在审问这个嫌疑犯。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhèngzài shěnwèn zhège xiányífàn.
examples.english: The police are interrogating this suspect.

examples.hanzi: 嫌疑犯已经逃跑了。
examples.pinyin: Xiányífàn yǐjīng táopǎo le.
examples.english: The suspect has already run away.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 迹 is a footprint, as in 奇迹 miracle.
亦 (yì) — near sound — 迹 is jì; 亦 also sounds out 迹 jì.
象 (elephant) — a picture of an elephant with trunk on top and legs below. 像 likeness adds 亻; 想象 imagine, 印象 impression use the "image" sense.

example.hanzi: 天空出现了暴风雨的迹象。
example.pinyin: Tiānkōng chūxiàn le bàofēngyǔ de jìxiàng.
example.english: Signs of a storm appeared in the sky.
example.fact: After the devastating 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami, wildlife officials in Sri Lanka's Yala National Park found remarkably few animal carcasses compared to the human toll. It led some researchers to suspect that elephants and other animals sensed the coming wave through ground vibrations and fled to higher ground well before it struck.

examples.hanzi: 医生说病人有好转的迹象。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō bìngrén yǒu hǎozhuǎn de jìxiàng.
examples.english: The doctor said the patient shows signs of improvement.

examples.hanzi: 目前还没有下雨的迹象。
examples.pinyin: Mùqián hái méiyǒu xià yǔ de jìxiàng.
examples.english: There are no signs of rain so far.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — gods, rites and blessings: 礼 ritual, 福 fortune, 祝 wish; here 神 god or spirit.
申 (shēn) gives the sound (shén, tone differs); also in 伸 shēn stretch and 绅 shēn.
圣 (holy) — traditional 聖 had an ear 耳 and a mouth 口: the sage who listens and speaks wisely.

example.hanzi: 教堂里的气氛显得十分神圣。
example.pinyin: Jiàotáng lǐ de qìfēn xiǎn de shífēn shénshèng.
example.english: The atmosphere inside the church felt very sacred.
example.fact: Mount Kailash in Tibet is considered sacred by four separate religions — Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, and Bon — and, out of respect for that shared religious significance, no one is known to have ever climbed to its summit; mountaineering on the peak is effectively forbidden.

examples.hanzi: 这座山对当地人来说非常神圣。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò shān duì dāngdì rén lái shuō fēicháng shénshèng.
examples.english: This mountain is sacred to the local people.

examples.hanzi: 他们在神圣的地方举行婚礼。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài shénshèng de dìfang jǔxíng hūnlǐ.
examples.english: They held their wedding in a sacred place.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 钅 is simplified 金 (metal), as in 钱, 铁, 银; 钻 is a drill, then a diamond.
占 (zhàn) — near sound — 钻 is zuān/zuàn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 战 zhàn.

example.hanzi: 老鼠钻进了洞里。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshǔ zuān jìn le dòng lǐ.
example.english: The mouse crept into the hole.
example.fact: 钻 has two readings: zuān is the verb 'to drill or squeeze into', while zuàn is the noun 'a drill, a diamond' as in 钻石. Don't mix them up: 钻进 (zuānjìn) means 'to burrow into'.

examples.hanzi: 他钻进了被子里。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuān jìn le bèizi li.
examples.english: He crawled into the quilt.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们从桌子下面钻过去。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen cóng zhuōzi xiàmiàn zuān guòqù.
examples.english: The kids crawled under the table.

components.note: 穴 (cave) — 穴 is a cave or hole, as in 窗 window, 穷 poor; 空 is empty like a hollow.
工 (gōng) — near sound — 空 is kōng; also in 红 hóng.
中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.

example.hanzi: 一只老鹰在空中盘旋。
example.pinyin: Yì zhī lǎoyīng zài kōngzhōng pánxuán.
example.english: An eagle circled in the air.
example.fact: A Rüppell's griffon vulture holds the confirmed record for highest flight of any bird, after colliding with an airplane at roughly 11,300 meters (37,000 feet) — about the cruising altitude of a commercial jet. The species' blood has an unusually high oxygen-binding efficiency that lets it function in such thin air.

examples.hanzi: 空中飘着一个红气球。
examples.pinyin: Kōngzhōng piāo zhe yí ge hóng qìqiú.
examples.english: A red balloon is floating in the air.

examples.hanzi: 飞机在空中飞行了五个小时。
examples.pinyin: Fēijī zài kōngzhōng fēixíng le wǔ ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: The plane flew for five hours in the air.

components.note: 广 (building) — 广 is a building radical, as in 店, 床; 度 also sounds out 渡 dù and 镀 dù.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 假 is to borrow or fake, a person lending a false front.
叚 (jiǎ) sounds like 假; also in 暇 xiá and 霞 xiá.

example.hanzi: 我们打算去海边度假一周。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen dǎsuàn qù hǎibiān dùjià yì zhōu.
example.english: We plan to go to the seaside for a week's vacation.
example.fact: France was among the first countries to legally guarantee workers paid time off, introducing two weeks of mandatory paid leave in 1936 under the Matignon Agreements. The entitlement has since grown to five weeks and helped establish the modern idea of a paid vacation as a basic labor right across much of Europe.

examples.hanzi: 暑假我们全家去海边度假。
examples.pinyin: Shǔjià wǒmen quánjiā qù hǎibiān dùjià.
examples.english: In the summer vacation, our whole family goes to the seaside for a holiday.

examples.hanzi: 他正在国外度假，不在办公室。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhèngzài guówài dùjià, bú zài bàngōngshì.
examples.english: He's on vacation abroad and isn't in the office.

components.note: 正 (zhèng) is a close sound clue for zhěng; 正 also means correct, fitting for putting things in order.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: setting things right by force.
正 (zhèng) is a close sound clue for zhěng; 正 also means correct, fitting for putting things in order.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: setting things right by force.

example.hanzi: 他为这次考试准备了整整一年。
example.pinyin: Tā wèi zhè cì kǎoshì zhǔnbèi le zhěngzhěng yì nián.
example.english: He spent a whole year preparing for this exam.
example.fact: A solar day and a sidereal day are not quite the same length: Earth actually completes one full 360-degree spin in about 23 hours and 56 minutes, four minutes short of the familiar 24-hour day. Those extra minutes are needed because Earth also has to turn a bit further to catch up with its own movement around the Sun.

examples.hanzi: 我等了整整两个小时。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ děng le zhěngzhěng liǎng ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: I waited a full two hours.

examples.hanzi: 这本书我整整看了一个月。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū wǒ zhěngzhěng kàn le yí ge yuè.
examples.english: It took me a whole month to read this book.

components.note: 舟 (boat) — 舟 is a boat, as in 船, 般; 航 is sailing.
亢 (kàng) — near sound — 航 is háng; 亢 also sounds out 抗 kàng and 坑 kēng.
穴 (cave) — 穴 is a cave or hole, as in 窗 window, 穷 poor; 空 is empty like a hollow.
工 (gōng) — near sound — 空 is kōng; also in 红 hóng.

example.hanzi: 他在一家航空公司当飞行员。
example.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā hángkōng gōngsī dāng fēixíngyuán.
example.english: He works as a pilot at an aviation company.
example.fact: The Wright brothers' first powered flight in 1903 covered only about 120 feet — shorter than the wingspan of a modern Boeing 747. Brief as it was, it marked the first time in history that a heavier-than-air machine carried a person under its own power.

examples.hanzi: 我哥哥在航空公司上班。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge zài hángkōng gōngsī shàngbān.
examples.english: My older brother works at an airline.

examples.hanzi: 这个城市有一所航空学校。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì yǒu yì suǒ hángkōng xuéxiào.
examples.english: This city has an aviation school.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 探 is to reach out and feel, then to explore.
The right half is a sound part shared with 深 shēn: a loose clue for tàn.
长 (long, grow) — simplified from 長, an old person with long hair. Read cháng "long" or zhǎng "to grow, elder".

example.hanzi: 探长仔细检查了案发现场。
example.pinyin: Tànzhǎng zǐxì jiǎnchá le ànfā xiànchǎng.
example.english: The detective carefully examined the crime scene.
example.fact: London's Metropolitan Police created its first plainclothes Detective Branch in 1842, more than a decade after uniformed officers began patrolling the streets in 1829. The delay partly reflected public unease about police who didn't announce themselves, which many at the time equated with spying.

examples.hanzi: 探长问了目击者几个问题。
examples.pinyin: Tànzhǎng wèn le mùjīzhě jǐ ge wèntí.
examples.english: The detective asked the eyewitness a few questions.

examples.hanzi: 这位探长破了很多大案子。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi tànzhǎng pò le hěn duō dà ànzi.
examples.english: This detective has solved many big cases.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).
火 (fire) — a picture of flames, and a component seen in 烧, 灯, 热 (as the dots 灬), 炒; fire radical for burning and heat.

example.hanzi: 士兵接到命令后立刻开火。
example.pinyin: Shìbīng jiēdào mìnglìng hòu lìkè kāihuǒ.
example.english: The soldiers opened fire immediately after receiving the order.
example.fact: During the informal Christmas Truce of 1914, soldiers on opposing sides of World War I's Western Front spontaneously stopped shooting, sang carols across the trenches, and in some sections even played football in no-man's land before the fighting resumed days later.

examples.hanzi: 对方突然开火，我们只好撤退。
examples.pinyin: Duìfāng tūrán kāihuǒ, wǒmen zhǐhǎo chètuì.
examples.english: The other side suddenly opened fire, so we had to retreat.

examples.hanzi: 没有命令，谁也不许开火。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu mìnglìng, shéi yě bù xǔ kāihuǒ.
examples.english: No one is allowed to open fire without orders.

components.note: 仓 (cāng) — granary; as a part it sounds out 苍 cāng, 沧 cāng and 舱 cāng.
广 (building) — marks halls and shelters, as in 店, 座, 床; 库 is a storehouse, here for carts 车.

example.hanzi: 这些货物存放在仓库里。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē huòwù cúnfàng zài cāngkù lǐ.
example.english: These goods are stored in the warehouse.
example.fact: Boeing's factory in Everett, Washington, is one of the largest buildings in the world by volume, covering roughly 98 acres under a single roof. It's so large that employees use bicycles and small trains just to move between different sections of the assembly line.

examples.hanzi: 仓库里堆满了箱子。
examples.pinyin: Cāngkù lǐ duī mǎn le xiāngzi.
examples.english: The warehouse is piled full of boxes.

examples.hanzi: 他在仓库里整理货物。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài cāngkù lǐ zhěnglǐ huòwù.
examples.english: He's organizing goods in the warehouse.

components.note: 吉 (jí) — lucky; as a part it sounds out 结 jié and 洁 jié.
亻 (person) — marks people, as in 你 you, 们 plural, 做 do; 他 is "he" (or other).
也 (yě) is only a loose sound hint for tā; the sibling 她 tā (she) shares it with 女 for woman.

example.hanzi: 他每天晚上都练习弹吉他。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān wǎnshang dōu liànxí tán jítā.
example.english: He practices playing the guitar every evening.
example.fact: The guitar's ancestors stretch back over 3,000 years to stringed instruments found in ancient Mesopotamia and Egypt, long predating the modern six-string design that only took its familiar shape in 19th-century Spain, thanks largely to luthier Antonio de Torres Jurado.

examples.hanzi: 我想学弹吉他。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xué tán jítā.
examples.english: I want to learn to play the guitar.

examples.hanzi: 他送了我一把新吉他。
examples.pinyin: Tā sòng le wǒ yì bǎ xīn jítā.
examples.english: He gave me a new guitar.

components.note: 石 (stone) — stones and minerals: 破, 研, 砖; 码 first meant stone weights, then numbers.
马 (mǎ) sounds exactly like 码; also in 吗, 骂 mà, 妈 mā.
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.

example.hanzi: 渔船缓缓靠近了码头。
example.pinyin: Yúchuán huǎnhuǎn kàojìn le mǎtou.
example.english: The fishing boat slowly approached the dock.
example.fact: The Port of Shanghai has been the world's busiest container port every year since 2010, handling more than 47 million shipping containers annually — over three times the volume moved by the busiest port in the United States.

examples.hanzi: 货船已经停在码头边了。
examples.pinyin: Huòchuán yǐjīng tíng zài mǎtou biān le.
examples.english: The cargo ship has already docked at the wharf.

examples.hanzi: 我们在码头等渡轮。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài mǎtou děng dùlún.
examples.english: We're waiting for the ferry at the dock.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过 pass, 进 enter, 送 send; to follow is to move along behind someone.
著 (zhù / zhe) — older form of 着: 艹 plant + 者 (zhě) as sound. 着 is a variant with 羊 over 目; neither part gives the 'in progress' sense.
目 (eye) — the bottom. The eye family: 看, 眼, 睛, 睡. In 着 it is only part of a variant shape. Memory aid: 睡着 — eyes 目 shut, asleep.

example.hanzi: 随着科技的发展,生活越来越方便。
example.pinyin: Suízhe kējì de fāzhǎn, shēnghuó yuè lái yuè fāngbiàn.
example.english: With the development of technology, life is becoming more and more convenient.
example.fact: Starling flocks perform a phenomenon called a murmuration, in which thousands of birds shift direction almost simultaneously. Researchers have found each bird isn't reacting to the whole flock at once — it's simply tracking and instantly following the movements of its seven closest neighbors, which is enough to make the whole group move as one.

examples.hanzi: 随着年龄的增长，他变得越来越成熟。
examples.pinyin: Suízhe niánlíng de zēngzhǎng, tā biàn de yuè lái yuè chéngshú.
examples.english: As he grows older, he becomes more and more mature.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们随着音乐跳起舞来。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen suízhe yīnyuè tiào qǐ wǔ lái.
examples.english: The children began dancing along with the music.

components.note: 广 (shelter) — buildings, as in 店, 床, 度: a hall or courtyard.
廷 (tíng) gives the exact sound; also in 挺 tǐng and 艇 tǐng.

example.hanzi: 孩子们在庭院里玩。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zài tíngyuàn lǐ wán.
example.english: The children are playing in the courtyard.
example.fact: 庭 started as a courtyard or palace hall, and the sense of 'court' extended to the family (家庭) and to a court of law (法庭). It is seldom a free-standing word and mostly appears in such compounds.

examples.hanzi: 我们的家庭很幸福。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de jiātíng hěn xìngfú.
examples.english: Our family is very happy.

examples.hanzi: 他今天要去法庭作证。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān yào qù fǎtíng zuòzhèng.
examples.english: He is going to testify in court today.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — heads and faces: 头, 额 forehead, 题 title, 领 collar; 顺 is a head following the river 川 along.
川 (chuān) is only a loose sound hint; 训 xùn and 顺 shùn share it.

example.hanzi: 今天的工作很顺。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān de gōngzuò hěn shùn.
example.english: Work went smoothly today.
example.fact: 顺 turns up in many greetings and set phrases, such as 一路顺风 ('smooth sailing') and 顺便 ('by the way, while you're at it'). As a verb, 顺着 means 'along', as in 顺着这条路走.

examples.hanzi: 祝你一路顺风!
examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ yílù shùnfēng!
examples.english: Have a good trip!

examples.hanzi: 这条路顺着河一直走就到了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù shùn zhe hé yìzhí zǒu jiù dào le.
examples.english: Follow the river along this road and you'll get there.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — marks actions, as in 教, 改, 放; 散 is to scatter (sàn) or to be loose (sǎn).

example.hanzi: 会议结束了，大家都散了。
example.pinyin: Huìyì jiéshù le, dàjiā dōu sàn le.
example.english: The meeting is over and everyone has dispersed.
example.fact: 散 has two readings: sàn is the verb 'to scatter or break up', as in 散步 'go for a stroll', while sǎn means 'loose, in pieces', as in 散装 (sold loose) or 散文 (prose).

examples.hanzi: 周末我喜欢在公园散步。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ xǐhuan zài gōngyuán sànbù.
examples.english: On weekends I like to take a walk in the park.

examples.hanzi: 雾慢慢地散了。
examples.pinyin: Wù mànmàn de sàn le.
examples.english: The fog slowly cleared.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: to drive away, set free.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fàng; 方 also in 房 fáng and 访 fǎng.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.hanzi: 请把书放到桌子上。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shū fàngdào zhuōzi shàng.
example.english: Please put the book onto the table.
example.fact: The Crypt of Civilization at Oglethorpe University in Georgia, sealed shut in 1940, is often called the first modern time capsule. It isn't scheduled to be opened until the year 8113 — nearly 6,000 years after it was placed there, chosen to mark an equal span of time before and after the start of the Egyptian calendar.

examples.hanzi: 请把衣服放到洗衣机里。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ yīfu fàng dào xǐyījī lǐ.
examples.english: Please put the clothes into the washing machine.

examples.hanzi: 他把行李放到了车后面。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ xíngli fàng dào le chē hòumiàn.
examples.english: He put the luggage at the back of the car.

components.note: 工 (work, craft) — craft and skill — clever handiwork; also in 左, 差.
丂 (kǎo) — near sound — 巧 qiǎo; 丂 also sounds out 考 kǎo and 烤 kǎo.
合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.

example.hanzi: 我们在同一天生日,真是巧合。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài tóng yì tiān shēngrì, zhēnshi qiǎohé.
example.english: We have the same birthday — what a coincidence.
example.fact: The 'birthday paradox' shows that in a random group of just 23 people, there is better than a 50% chance two of them share a birthday. Most people badly underestimate this because they instinctively compare their own birthday to everyone else's, rather than counting every possible pair in the group.

examples.hanzi: 这真是一个巧合。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhēn shì yí ge qiǎohé.
examples.english: This is really a coincidence.

examples.hanzi: 我们在国外遇到，真巧合！
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài guówài yùdào, zhēn qiǎohé!
examples.english: We ran into each other abroad, what a coincidence!

components.note: 山 (mountain) — a picture of three peaks; as a radical it marks hills, as in 岛, 峰, 岸.
女 (woman) — 女 marks women and female roles, as in 妈 mom, 姐 sister, 姑 aunt; 姆 is a nanny, as in 保姆.
母 (mǔ) — same sound — 姆 is mǔ, just like 母 (mother).

example.hanzi: 山姆每天早上都去跑步。
example.pinyin: Shānmǔ měitiān zǎoshang dōu qù pǎobù.
example.english: Sam goes jogging every morning.
example.fact: The American nickname 'Uncle Sam' is generally traced to Samuel Wilson, a meatpacker who supplied barrels of beef stamped 'U.S.' to American troops during the War of 1812. Soldiers reportedly joked that the initials stood for 'Uncle Sam' Wilson himself, and the nickname for the country stuck.

examples.hanzi: 山姆是我的新邻居。
examples.pinyin: Shānmǔ shì wǒ de xīn línjū.
examples.english: Sam is my new neighbor.

examples.hanzi: 我昨天遇到了山姆，他刚回国。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān yùdào le Shānmǔ, tā gāng huíguó.
examples.english: I ran into Sam yesterday; he just got back to the country.

components.note: 酉 (wine jar) — marks wine and brewing, as in 酒, 醉 drunk, 醒; 配 first meant mixing wine, then matching.
己 (jǐ) is only a loose sound hint for pèi.
合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.

example.hanzi: 团队成员之间配合得很好。
example.pinyin: Tuánduì chéngyuán zhījiān pèihé de hěn hǎo.
example.english: The team members cooperate very well with each other.
example.fact: Cleaner wrasse fish run informal 'cleaning stations' on coral reefs, where much larger predatory fish line up and hold perfectly still while the wrasse picks parasites off their skin and even out of their mouths and gills — a mutual arrangement that benefits both species without the predator eating its cleaner.

examples.hanzi: 谢谢你的配合。
examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ de pèihé.
examples.english: Thank you for your cooperation.

examples.hanzi: 他们配合得很默契。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen pèihé de hěn mòqì.
examples.english: They work together with great chemistry.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — marks grain and crops, as in 秋, 种, 租; 称 originally meant weighing grain, then naming (称呼).
口 (mouth) — breath and speech: 吸, 叫, 喊; 呼 is to breathe out or call.
乎 (hū) sounds exactly like 呼.

example.hanzi: 你可以直接称呼我的名字。
example.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ zhíjiē chēnghu wǒ de míngzi.
example.english: You can just address me by my first name.
example.fact: Queen Elizabeth II reigned for over 70 years, making her the longest-reigning monarch in British history when she died in 2022. During that single reign, thirteen different U.S. presidents and fifteen different British prime ministers came and went while the formal address for the British sovereign remained unchanged.

examples.hanzi: 我们应该怎么称呼您？
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi zěnme chēnghu nín?
examples.english: How should we address you?

examples.hanzi: 大家都称呼他为老王。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu chēnghu tā wéi Lǎo Wáng.
examples.english: Everyone calls him Lao Wang.

components.note: 女 (woman) — a person kneeling with arms crossed; as a radical it heads many female and family words: 妈, 好, 姐.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 那位女子正在图书馆看书。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi nǚzǐ zhèngzài túshūguǎn kànshū.
example.english: That woman is reading in the library.
example.fact: Marie Curie remains the only person of any gender to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences — physics in 1903 and chemistry in 1911 — for her pioneering research on radioactivity, a term she herself coined.

examples.hanzi: 这位女子是新来的老师。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi nǚzǐ shì xīn lái de lǎoshī.
examples.english: This woman is the new teacher.

examples.hanzi: 一名女子在车站捡到了钱包。
examples.pinyin: Yì míng nǚzǐ zài chēzhàn jiǎn dào le qiánbāo.
examples.english: A woman found a wallet at the station.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 怀 is to cherish something in the heart or bosom.
不 (bù) only stands in for the complicated sound part of traditional 懷 (huái); a loose clue.

example.hanzi: 她怀着梦想来到北京。
example.pinyin: Tā huáizhe mèngxiǎng lái dào Běijīng.
example.english: She came to Beijing cherishing a dream.
example.fact: 怀 as a verb means 'to carry in one's chest or heart', so it links both the physical (怀孕, pregnant) and the emotional (怀念, to long for someone gone). It goes with abstract nouns such as 怀着希望 'full of hope'.

examples.hanzi: 我很怀念小时候的生活。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn huáiniàn xiǎoshíhou de shēnghuó.
examples.english: I really miss my childhood life.

examples.hanzi: 她怀了一个宝宝。
examples.pinyin: Tā huái le yí ge bǎobao.
examples.english: She is expecting a baby.

components.note: 具 (tool) — two hands 廾 (the bottom 八) hold something valuable above — to provide, and a tool, as in 工具; 具 also sounds out 惧 jù.
月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.

example.hanzi: 这种材料具有防水的功能。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng cáiliào jùyǒu fángshuǐ de gōngnéng.
example.english: This material has a waterproof function.
example.fact: Axolotls possess a remarkable regenerative ability: they can regrow entire lost limbs, sections of their spinal cord, and even parts of their heart and brain without forming any scar tissue. That ability has made them one of the most heavily studied model organisms in regenerative medicine research.

examples.hanzi: 这个手机具有很多新功能。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shǒujī jùyǒu hěn duō xīn gōngnéng.
examples.english: This phone has a lot of new features.

examples.hanzi: 她具有很强的领导能力。
examples.pinyin: Tā jùyǒu hěn qiáng de lǐngdǎo nénglì.
examples.english: She has strong leadership ability.

meanings: (coll.) admirable, impressive (usu. in 好样的, 'way to go')

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌 table, 板 board; 样 once meant a tree (acorn) and later "form, pattern".
羊 (yáng, sheep) is a near-exact sound clue for yàng; 羊 also sounds out 洋 yáng and 养 yǎng.

example.hanzi: 面对困难还能坚持下去,真是好样的。
example.pinyin: Miànduì kùnnán hái néng jiānchí xiàqù, zhēnshi hǎoyàng de.
example.english: Being able to keep going in the face of difficulty — now that's admirable.
example.fact: Junko Tabei survived being buried in an avalanche partway up a mountain in 1970, and just five years later, in 1975, became the first woman to reach the summit of Mount Everest. She went on to become the first woman to complete the Seven Summits, climbing the highest peak on every continent.

examples.hanzi: 你今天考得这么好，真是好样的！
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān kǎo de zhème hǎo, zhēn shì hǎoyàng de!
examples.english: You did so well on the test today, way to go!

examples.hanzi: 他们是好样的，从不放弃。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen shì hǎoyàng de, cóng bù fàngqì.
examples.english: They're admirable folks who never give up.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
子 (child) — 了 is usually read as a swaddled baby, like 子 without the arms. Its meanings 'finish' (了解 liǎo) and the particle le were borrowed later.

example.hanzi: 就算失败了也没什么大不了的。
example.pinyin: Jiùsuàn shībài le yě méi shénme dàbuliǎo de.
example.english: Even if we fail, it's really no big deal.
example.fact: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault, built into an Arctic mountainside, was engineered to survive almost any worst-case scenario, including a direct nuclear strike. It currently holds backup samples of more than a million crop seed varieties, insurance against the possibility of a global agricultural catastrophe.

examples.hanzi: 大不了重新做一遍。
examples.pinyin: Dàbuliǎo chóngxīn zuò yí biàn.
examples.english: At worst, we'll just redo it.

examples.hanzi: 迟到一会儿没什么大不了的。
examples.pinyin: Chídào yíhuìr méi shénme dàbuliǎo de.
examples.english: Being a little late is no big deal.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 别: hard enough to cut.
冈 (gāng) gives the exact sound; also in 钢 gāng and 纲 gāng.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.

example.hanzi: 这双鞋的尺寸刚好合适。
example.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié de chǐcùn gānghǎo héshì.
example.english: This pair of shoes fits exactly right.
example.fact: Earth orbits the Sun within what astronomers call the 'Goldilocks zone,' the narrow band of distance where temperatures are just right for liquid water to exist on a planet's surface. Climate models suggest that moving Earth even a few percent closer to the Sun could trigger a runaway greenhouse effect that boils away the oceans entirely.

examples.hanzi: 我到车站时，车刚好开走了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dào chēzhàn shí, chē gānghǎo kāi zǒu le.
examples.english: When I got to the station, the bus had just left.

examples.hanzi: 这些钱刚好够买一本书。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē qián gānghǎo gòu mǎi yì běn shū.
examples.english: This money is just enough to buy a book.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a tree with a mark at the base: the root, hence source, origin, and the measure word for books.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 申请人必须本人到场办理手续。
example.pinyin: Shēnqǐngrén bìxū běnrén dàochǎng bànlǐ shǒuxù.
example.english: The applicant must be present in person to complete the procedures.
example.fact: Very few animal species reliably pass the mirror self-recognition test, which checks whether an animal understands it's looking at its own reflection rather than another individual. Only a handful of species — including great apes, dolphins, elephants, and Eurasian magpies — have been shown to pass it convincingly.

examples.hanzi: 本人亲自到现场检查了。
examples.pinyin: Běnrén qīnzì dào xiànchǎng jiǎnchá le.
examples.english: I personally went to the site to inspect it.

examples.hanzi: 照片上的人和本人很像。
examples.pinyin: Zhàopiàn shàng de rén hé běnrén hěn xiàng.
examples.english: The person in the photo looks a lot like the real person.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — marks cloth, as in 衬, 衫, 裤; 补 is to mend a garment.
卜 (bǔ) gives the sound exactly: 补 bǔ.
亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 做, 借; 偿 is to repay.
尝 (cháng) gives the sound exactly: 偿 cháng.

example.hanzi: 公司决定给受影响的顾客一些补偿。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī juédìng gěi shòu yǐngxiǎng de gùkè yìxiē bǔcháng.
example.english: The company decided to give the affected customers some compensation.
example.fact: Many people who lose their eyesight show measurable improvement in their remaining senses, a phenomenon researchers call sensory compensation. Brain-imaging studies have found the visual cortex — normally dedicated to processing sight — gets recruited to help process sound and touch instead.

examples.hanzi: 航空公司会补偿你的损失。
examples.pinyin: Hángkōng gōngsī huì bǔcháng nǐ de sǔnshī.
examples.english: The airline will compensate you for your loss.

examples.hanzi: 我想补偿一下孩子，周末带他出去玩。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bǔcháng yíxià háizi, zhōumò dài tā chūqù wán.
examples.english: I want to make it up to my child by taking him out this weekend.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — marks feelings, as in 情, 快, 怕; 忏 is remorse.
千 (qiān) is only a loose sound hint for chàn.
忄 (heart) — 忄 is the heart radical for feelings, as in 情, 怕; 悔 is regret.
每 (měi) — loose hint — 悔 is huǐ; 每 also sounds out 梅 méi and 海 hǎi.

example.hanzi: 他在信中表达了深深的忏悔。
example.pinyin: Tā zài xìn zhōng biǎodá le shēnshēn de chànhuǐ.
example.english: In the letter, he expressed deep repentance.
example.fact: South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission, set up in 1995 after the end of apartheid, offered perpetrators of political violence amnesty from prosecution in exchange for a full public confession of their crimes. The restorative-justice model it pioneered has since been studied and partly adapted by more than 40 other countries.

examples.hanzi: 他向老师忏悔，承认自己作弊了。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàng lǎoshī chànhuǐ, chéngrèn zìjǐ zuòbì le.
examples.english: He repented to the teacher, admitting he had cheated.

examples.hanzi: 她常去教堂忏悔。
examples.pinyin: Tā cháng qù jiàotáng chànhuǐ.
examples.english: She often goes to church to confess.

components.note: ⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and walking: 跑, 路, 跳; 跟 first meant the heel, then to follow.
艮 (gèn) is a near sound match for gēn; same part in 根 gēn, 很 hěn, 恨 hèn.
著 (zhù / zhe) — older form of 着: 艹 plant + 者 (zhě) as sound. 着 is a variant with 羊 over 目; neither part gives the 'in progress' sense.
目 (eye) — the bottom. The eye family: 看, 眼, 睛, 睡. In 着 it is only part of a variant shape. Memory aid: 睡着 — eyes 目 shut, asleep.

example.hanzi: 小狗一直跟着主人跑来跑去。
example.pinyin: Xiǎogǒu yìzhí gēnzhe zhǔrén pǎo lái pǎo qù.
example.english: The little dog kept following its owner around.
example.fact: Konrad Lorenz's studies of graylag geese in the 1930s revealed 'imprinting': goslings will follow the first moving object they see after hatching and treat it as their mother. In his most famous demonstrations, goslings imprinted on Lorenz himself and followed him everywhere, work that later earned him a share of the 1973 Nobel Prize.

examples.hanzi: 你先走，我马上跟着你。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān zǒu, wǒ mǎshàng gēnzhe nǐ.
examples.english: You go first; I'll follow you right away.

examples.hanzi: 我跟着视频学做饭。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēnzhe shìpín xué zuòfàn.
examples.english: I'm learning to cook by following a video.

components.note: 日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.
日 (sun) — time and day, as in 时, 晚, 明: the sun at the top of a sprout, early morning. 早 also gives 草 cǎo and 澡 zǎo.

example.hanzi: 明早八点我们要出发去机场。
example.pinyin: Míngzǎo bā diǎn wǒmen yào chūfā qù jīchǎng.
example.english: Tomorrow morning at eight o'clock we need to leave for the airport.
example.fact: The 2017 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine went to three scientists who identified the genes controlling the body's circadian clock, the internal timer that makes many people feel groggy at dawn and alert by mid-morning. Their research traced the rhythm to a feedback loop of proteins that rise and fall roughly every 24 hours, even in constant darkness. This same clock is why jet lag disrupts sleep after crossing time zones.

examples.hanzi: 你明早有时间吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ míngzǎo yǒu shíjiān ma?
examples.english: Do you have time tomorrow morning?

examples.hanzi: 我们明早在门口见面吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen míngzǎo zài ménkǒu jiànmiàn ba.
examples.english: Let's meet at the entrance tomorrow morning.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo slips, once used for writing and lists, as in 等 wait, 笔 pen, 笑 laugh.
弟 (dì) gives the exact sound; 弟 also sounds out 梯 tī and 剃 tì.
亠 (lid) — the top stroke group, as in 市 and 交. The sound-borrowed number; no meaning link. Memory aid: a lid on top of 八 (eight) ends up as six.
八 (eight) — the bottom part, as in 分 divide. Same shape as 'eight' but the number 六 does not come from it; use it as a visual memory aid.

example.hanzi: 他在班里排名第六。
example.pinyin: Tā zài bān lǐ páimíng dì liù.
example.english: He ranks sixth in his class.
example.fact: Many biologists argue Earth is now in the midst of a sixth mass extinction, following five prehistoric die-offs including the one that ended the dinosaurs 66 million years ago. Unlike those earlier events, which were driven by asteroid impacts or volcanic activity, the current wave of species loss is linked mainly to habitat destruction, climate change, and overexploitation by humans. Some estimates suggest species are vanishing at tens to hundreds of times the natural background rate.

examples.hanzi: 今天是我第六次来这里。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shì wǒ dì liù cì lái zhèlǐ.
examples.english: This is the sixth time I've come here.

examples.hanzi: 请翻到第六页。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng fān dào dìliù yè.
examples.english: Please turn to page six.

components.note: 自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).
彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.
车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.

example.hanzi: 我每天骑自行车去上班。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān qí zìxíngchē qù shàngbān.
example.english: I ride my bicycle to work every day.
example.fact: Pound for pound, the bicycle is one of the most energy-efficient machines ever built: a cyclist converts roughly a quarter of their pedaling energy into forward motion, far more efficient than walking or driving. In the 1980s, China had so many bicycles on its roads that it earned the nickname 'the Kingdom of Bicycles,' with hundreds of millions of riders at the time.

examples.hanzi: 我的自行车坏了，得去修一修。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de zìxíngchē huài le, děi qù xiū yi xiū.
examples.english: My bike is broken; I need to get it repaired.

examples.hanzi: 周末我们骑自行车去郊外。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qí zìxíngchē qù jiāowài.
examples.english: This weekend we're cycling to the countryside.

components.note: 壴 (zhù, drum) — a drum on top of 口 mouth: music and singing, joy.
口 (mouth) — singing and speaking, as in 唱 sing, 吃 eat.

example.hanzi: 恭喜你考上了大学！
example.pinyin: Gōngxǐ nǐ kǎo shàng le dàxué!
example.english: Congratulations on getting into university!
example.fact: 喜 is the root of 喜欢 'to like' and 恭喜 'congratulations', and a doubled form 囍 is a classic wedding decoration. As a free word it is mostly set-phrase, as in 喜事 'a happy event' and 报喜 'to announce good news'.

examples.hanzi: 你喜欢喝茶还是咖啡?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan hē chá háishi kāfēi?
examples.english: Do you like tea or coffee?

examples.hanzi: 他们的婚礼办得很喜庆。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen de hūnlǐ bàn de hěn xǐqìng.
examples.english: Their wedding was very festive.

components.note: 犭 (animal) — 犭 is the animal radical, as in 猫, 狗, 狼; 犹 first named an animal.
尤 (yóu) — same sound — 犹 is yóu, like 尤; 尤 also sounds out 优 yōu.
大 (big) — an extra stroke below emphasises it: bigger than big, too much. 太 also sounds out 泰 tài.

example.hanzi: 他的犹太祖先在二十世纪初移民到了美国。
example.pinyin: Tā de Yóutài zǔxiān zài èrshí shìjì chū yímín dàole Měiguó.
example.english: His Jewish ancestors immigrated to the United States in the early twentieth century.
example.fact: The Dead Sea Scrolls, a collection of ancient Jewish texts including the oldest known copies of the Hebrew Bible, were discovered largely by chance in 1947 when a Bedouin shepherd threw a rock into a cave near Qumran and heard it shatter pottery. The roughly 900 manuscripts, dated from the third century BC to the first century AD, were preserved for two millennia by the region's extremely dry climate.

examples.hanzi: 我的邻居是一位犹太老人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de línjū shì yí wèi Yóutài lǎorén.
examples.english: My neighbor is an elderly Jewish man.

examples.hanzi: 她在博物馆里了解了犹太文化。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bówùguǎn lǐ liǎojiě le Yóutài wénhuà.
examples.english: She learned about Jewish culture at the museum.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 标 first meant the tip of a tree, hence a mark or target; wood radical as in 树 tree, 板 board.
票 (piào) is the sound in traditional 標; same series 漂 piāo and 飘 piāo; simplified 标 now shows 示.
心 (heart) — feelings and will: 想, 思, 感; 志 is what the heart is set on, ambition.
士 (shì) is only a loose sound hint for zhì.

example.hanzi: 熊猫是中国的国家标志之一。
example.pinyin: Xióngmāo shì Zhōngguó de guójiā biāozhì zhī yī.
example.english: The panda is one of China's national symbols.
example.fact: The Nike 'swoosh' logo, now one of the most recognized brand marks in the world, was designed in 1971 by graphic design student Carolyn Davidson, who was paid just $35 for the work. Nike's founder reportedly wasn't thrilled with it at first, but the company later gave Davidson stock as thanks once the brand took off.

examples.hanzi: 红灯是停车的标志。
examples.pinyin: Hóngdēng shì tíngchē de biāozhì.
examples.english: A red light is the sign to stop.

examples.hanzi: 这个标志是什么意思？
examples.pinyin: Zhège biāozhì shì shénme yìsi?
examples.english: What does this sign mean?

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 住, 做.
木 (tree) — a person 亻 leaning on a tree 木: resting, hence 休息 rest and 退休 retire.

example.hanzi: 工作了一天，他想休息一下。
example.pinyin: Gōngzuò le yì tiān, tā xiǎng xiūxi yíxià.
example.english: After working all day, he wants to rest a bit.
example.fact: 休 is rarely used alone for 'rest' in modern speech: you normally say 休息 or 休假 (take leave). It also appears in the stern phrase 休想, 'don't even think about it'.

examples.hanzi: 他明年就要退休了。
examples.pinyin: Tā míngnián jiù yào tuìxiū le.
examples.english: He is going to retire next year.

examples.hanzi: 你已经工作很久了,休一天假吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǐjīng gōngzuò hěn jiǔ le, xiū yì tiān jià ba.
examples.english: You've worked a long time; take a day off.
